data.title: The Barnacle Goose Myth
data.author: jamesgpearce
data.article_summary: 《 barnacle goose 神话》讲述的是关于灰雁（Branta leucopsis）和黑雁（Branta bernicla）繁殖习性的历史误解。该神话声称这些雁从藤壶（Cirripedia）中完全成形而出，或其他非蛋生的方式生成。该神话源于对鸟类迁徙模式的无知，并在中世纪通过修道院手稿和动物寓言集传播。早期文献如11世纪的《埃克塞特书》中的谜语也提及此神话。19世纪末，鸟类迁徙研究才揭示这些雁迁徙到格陵兰或北欧繁殖。有学者如Ray Lankester认为，公元前1600-1100年间的迈锡尼定居者可能已经知道此神话，并通过陶器上的绘画表现出来，展示了藤壶与雁的关联。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：日本都市传说的真实性及其衍生话题（关于藤壶的讨论）

不同观点：
• [usagisushi的观点] 认为这是一个 creepy（令人毛骨悚然的）日本都市神话。他描述了故事的内容：一个人在沙滩上弄伤膝盖后，医生发现他的髌骨里长出了藤壶。他还提到，这样的故事可能并不会让人起鸡皮疙瘩（goosebump-less）。

• [DrNosferatu的观点] 没有直接讨论都市传说的真实性，而是转而谈论藤壶的美味，尤其是新鲜的藤壶。这似乎是在用幽默的方式回应前者的评论，将话题从都市传说的恐怖感转移到食物上。

补充讨论：
• 第一个评论集中于都市传说的内容及其带来的心理感受（ creepy, goosebump-less）。
• 第二个评论则偏离了恐怖感，引入了与食物相关的话题，制造了一种意外的转折。
• 两者之间的讨论焦点并不完全一致，前者关注传说的惊悚性，而后者关注传说的某个元素（藤壶）在现实中的属性（可食用性）。
• 争议的焦点可能在于对都市传说的态度：一个是认真对待其惊悚效果，另一个则是轻松看待并引入现实生活中的元素。

43431881.article_content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
Sources of ancient myth
From Topographia Hibernica British Library MS 13 B VIII (
c.
1188 CE
)
The
barnacle goose myth
is a widely-reported historical misconception about the breeding habits of the
barnacle goose
(
Branta leucopsis
) and
brant goose
(
Branta bernicla
).
[
1
]
One version of the myth is that these geese emerge fully formed from
goose barnacles
(
Cirripedia
).
[
2
]
Other myths exist about how the barnacle goose supposedly emerges and grows from matter other than bird eggs.
The etymology of the term "barnacle" suggests  Latin, Old English, and French roots.
[
3
]
There are few references in pre-Christian books and manuscripts – some Roman or Greek. The main vector for the myth into modern times was monastic manuscripts and in particular the
bestiary
.
[
4
]
The myth owes its long-standing popularity to an early ignorance of the migration patterns of geese. Early medieval discussions of the nature of living organisms were often based on myths or genuine ignorance of what is now known about phenomena such as
bird migration
. It was not until the late 19th century that bird migration research showed that such geese migrate northwards to nest and breed in Greenland or northern Scandinavia.
[
5
]
[
6
]
Early references
[
edit
]
An early, but not the first reference to the myth of the barnacle goose, is in the eleventh century
Exeter Book
of Riddles.
[
7
]
The riddle NUMBER 10, is asked as follows:
Neb wæs min on nearwe,         ond ic neoþan wætre,
flode underflowen,         firgenstreamum
swiþe besuncen,         ond on sunde awox
ufan yþum þeaht,         anum getenge
liþendum wuda         lice mine.
Hæfde feorh cwico,         þa ic of fæðmum cwom
brimes ond beames         on blacum hrægle;
sume wæron hwite         hyrste mine,
þa mec lifgende         lyft upp ahof,
wind of wæge,         siþþan wide bær
ofer seolhbaþo.         Saga hwæt ic hatte.
My nose was in a tight spot, and I beneath the water,
underflowed by the flood, sunk deep
into the ocean-waves, and in the sea grew
covered with waves from above, my body
touching a floating piece of wood.
I had living spirit, when I came out of the embrace
of water and wood in a black garment,
some of my trappings were white,
then the air lifted me, living, up,
wind from the water, then carried me far
over the seal's bath. Say what I am called.
To which the anticipated answer was "The Barnacle Goose".
[
8
]
In Ray Lankester's
Diversions of a Naturalist
(1917)
[
9
]
there is evidence of a serious literature debate arising from the work of
Max Muller
(1868),
[
10
]
together with a French Zoologist, Frederic Houssay,
[
11
]
George Perrot and
Charles Chipiez
.
[
12
]
The debate centered on the possibility that the barnacle goose myth could have been known to early Mycenaean settlers
c.
1600
–1100 BCE.
Lankester Fig 17 Diversions of a Naturalist  – Image from  " Ossuaire de Crète , Perrot "
Lankester claimed that drawings, often seen on Mycenaean pottery, were an
interpretation
by contemporary artists of the features of
typical geese
.  Lankester pointing out the way the Barnacle Geese were represented, wrote that the solution was:
The Mykenæan population of the islands of Cyprus and Crete, in the period 800 to 1000 years before Christ, were great makers of pottery, and painted large earthenware basins and vases with a variety of decorative representations of marine life, of fishes, butterflies, birds, and trees. … Others have been figured by the well-known archaeologists, … M. Perrot consulted M. Houssay, in his capacity of zoologist, in regard to these Mykenæan drawings, which bear … the evidence of having been designed after nature by one who knew the things in life, although they are not slavishly "copied" from nature…
He goes on to suggest that "it is fairly evident that the intention has been to manipulate the drawing of the leaf or fruit so as to make it resemble the drawing of the goose, whilst that in its turn is modified so as to emphasise or idealise its points of resemblance to a barnacle".
He summarises the possibility that Mycenaean drawings of birds – especially the goose – seen on pottery shows that the barnacle goose myth was known to settlers on the Greek islands, a thousand years BCE. He concludes his observations as follows:
… artists loved to exercise a little fancy and ingenuity. By gradual reduction in the number and size of outstanding parts—a common rule in the artistic "schematising" or "conventional simplification" of natural form—they converted the octopus and the argonaut, with their eight arms, into a bull's head with a pair of spiral horns … In the same spirit it seems that they observed and drew the barnacle floating on timber or thrown up after a storm on their shores. They detected a resemblance in the marking of its shells to the plumage of a goose, whilst in the curvature of its stalk they saw a resemblance to the long neck of the bird. … They brought the barnacle and the goose together

Scientists program stem cells to mimic first days of embryonic development
March 20, 2025
By
Emily Cerf
Share this story:
Twitter
Facebook
LinkedIn
Reddit
Programmable cellular models of embryos, known as embryoids, allow scientists to mimic the first few day of embryonic development.
The project team, left to right: Ali Shariati,
Sayaka Kozuki, and
Gerrald Lodewijk.
The earliest days after fertilization, once a sperm cell meets an egg, are shrouded in scientific mystery.
The process of how a humble single cell becomes an organism fascinates scientists across disciplines. For some animals, the entire process of cellular multiplication, generation of specialized cells, and their organization into an ordered multicellular embryo takes place in the protective environment of the uterus, making direct observation and studies challenging. This makes it difficult for scientists to understand what can go wrong during that process, and how specific risk factors and the surrounding environment may prevent embryo formation.
Scientists at UC Santa Cruz were able to engineer cellular models of embryos without ever experimenting with any actual embryos, allowing them to mimic the first few days after two sexually reproductive cells meet. They use CRISPR-based engineering methods to prompt stem cells to organize into “programmable” embryo-like structures, also known as embryoids, which can be used to study the role of certain genes in early development. These structures are not actual embryos but assemblies of lab-grown cells that self-organize in ways that mimic some aspects of early developmental stages.
Their results
are published in the leading stem cell journal
Cell Stem Cell
.
“We as scientists are interested in recreating and repurposing natural phenomena, such as formation of an embryo, in the dish to enable studies that are otherwise challenging to do with natural systems,” said Ali Shariati, assistant professor of biomolecular engineering and the study’s senior author. “We want to know how cells organize themselves into an embryo-like model, and what could go wrong when there are pathological conditions that prevent an embryo from successfully developing.”
Cell co-development
Shariati is an expert in stem cell engineering, a field that uses stem cells — unspecialized cells that can form any type of cell such as gut or brain cells — to study and solve biological and health problems.
This project, led by UCSC postdoctoral scholar Gerrald Lodewijk and biomolecular engineering alumna and current Caltech graduate student Sayaka Kozuki, used mouse stem cells that are commonly grown in the lab to guide them to form basic building blocks of the embryo.
The team used a version of CRISPR technology known as an epigenome editor, which does not cut DNA but instead modifies how it is expressed. They targeted regions of the genome known to be involved in the development of an early embryo. This allowed them to control which genes were activated, and induce the creation of main types of cells needed for early development.
“We use the stem cells, which are like a blank canvas, and use them to induce different cell types using our CRISPR tools,” Lodewijik said.
This method had the advantage of allowing different cell types to “co-develop,” which more closely resembles the natural embryo formation than the chemical approaches other scientists have used to develop different cell types.
“These cells co-develop together, just like they would in an actual embryo, and establish that history of being neighbors,” Shariati said. “We do not change their genome or expose them to specific signaling molecules, but rather activate the existing genes.”
The team found that 80% of the stem cells organize themselves into a structure that mimics the most basic form of an embryo after a few days, and most undergo gene activation that reflects the development process that occurs in living organisms.
“The similarity is remarkable in the way the cells organize themselves, as well as the molecular composition,” Shariati said. “[The cells require] very little input from us — it’s as if the cells already know what to do, and we just give them a little bit of guidance.”
The researchers observed that the cells showed a collective behavior in moving and organizing together.
“Some of them start doing this rotational migration, almost like the collective behavior of birds or other species,” Shariati said. “Through this collective behavior and migration they can form these fascinating embryonic patterns.”

data.author: Petiver
data.article_summary: 1850年代，楔形文字仍是未解之谜。四位学者展开竞争，试图破译这一古代书写系统，以揭示美索不达米亚文明的秘密。一块拥有3000年历史的 clay relic（泥板）成为焦点，它记录了亚述国王提格拉特·帕拉沙尔一世的军事胜利。最终，在大英博物馆的主持下，学者们取得了进展，逐渐解开了这一世界上最古老文字的奥秘。

data.title: CSS Form Control Styling Level 1 – W3C First Public Working Draft
data.author: tambourine_man
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种新的CSS属性`appearance: base`，旨在统一不同用户代理（浏览器）对表单控件的样式处理，解决以往样式不一致的问题。该属性使表单控件可以通过标准CSS和伪元素进行一致的样式定制，同时确保控件的可访问性和平台惯例。基本外观设计原则包括跨浏览器一致性、易于自定义、符合WCAG 2.2 AA标准、以及对不同模式和色彩方案的支持。文章还介绍了如何使用`appearance: base`来定制表单控件的外观，并讨论了`::picker()`伪元素，用于样式化表单控件的弹出部分，如选择框。总体目标是简化开发者对表单控件的自定义过程，同时保持其功能性和可访问性。

1.
Introduction
This section is non-normative.
User agents have long provided non-standard ways of styling form controls.
However, all of these controls are implemented inconsistently across user agents,
creating unnecessary friction for authors.
This module aims to define a set of form control parts in enough detail that
they can be used interoperably.
It also defines some new ways of customizing form controls,
covering common use cases that were previously only possible by
implementing custom controls from scratch, which was a lot of work,
hard to get right, and often broke either accessibility or platform conventions.
2.
Opting Into
Basic Appearance
: the
appearance: base
value
Move definition of
appearance
here.
Name:
appearance
New values:
base
When applied on a form control,
base
puts that control in the
basic appearance
state.
A control that has
basic appearance
is consistently styleable using standard CSS and the pseudo-elements defined below, and applies overridable default styles that are consistent across UAs.
When a control is in that state, the user agent applies styles from the
Appendix A: Basic Appearance User Agent Stylesheet
to that control.
The user agent must also enable the pseudo-elements defined by
§ 4 Pseudo-Elements
. These pseudo-elements (excluding
::picker()
) always
inherit
appearance
from their
originating element
. The user agent may implement this using an
appearance: inherit !important
declaration.
NOTE:
The inheritance prevents authors from mixing native and non-native parts for the same control.
2.1.
Design Principles for the
Basic Appearance
The following design principles apply to the design of the
basic appearance
stylesheet for form controls,
in order of descending importance:
The styles are identical in every user agent.
The controls are recognizable and usable on their own without additional styles.
The controls pass 100% of
WCAG 2.2 AA standards
.
The styles are consistent across controls…
…in look & feel.
…in how they are defined in code.
…in sizing and interaction.
The styles are easily adapted to the website’s branding, without needing complex reset stylesheets:
They use minimal code and are easy to override.
They do not have a strong voice & tone of their own, and are visually as simple as possible.
They inherit page styles rather than define new styles whenever possible.
They are resilient to adjustments…
…when changed themselves (e.g. changing font, border, layout).
…when put in context (e.g. ready to be flex or grid children).
They are comprehensive:
Covering all states for each control.
Supporting all writing modes and color schemes.
For HTML form controls specifically, these principles are applied through the required user agent stylesheet defined in
Appendix A: Basic Appearance User Agent Stylesheet
.
2.2.
Examples
Refine these examples through implementation, experimentation, bikeshedding and improvements to the user agent stylesheet.
The main purpose of these examples is to show how the design principles for the
basic appearance
apply in practice.

basic appearance
on individual controls, the following code is used:

不同观点：
• 一些美国人默许美国对格陵兰的兴趣，甚至公开支持吞并格陵兰，例如"all-in podcast"的成员。该观点提到，某些自由媒体的文章使用软实力手段，强调格陵兰人希望从丹麦独立的意愿，暗示美国在此问题上有一定的正当性。

• John Bolton等人物虽然批评特朗普的方式，但在原则上认为格陵兰应该属于美国，表明在美国政界也存在对扩张领土的潜在支持。

• 评论指出，反对美国对格陵兰兴趣的声音相对较小，暗示美国在此问题上有较大的操作空间。

• 评论将美国描述为一个寻求"Lebensraum im Norden"（北方的生存空间）的国家，并将美国定位为地缘政治中的主动挑衅者，认为美国试图通过挑起战争来削弱其盟友，并使欧盟和加拿大在美国与俄罗斯之间变得无关紧要。

• 提出加拿大和欧盟应组建联盟，并与俄罗斯达成和平协议。建议欧盟制定一个欧亚安全概念，排除美国，并确保欧亚大陆国家不被海洋国家拖入战争。加拿大应参与这一过程。

补充讨论：
• 评论暗示美国可能有更大的地缘政治目标，包括削弱其盟友和利用地缘政治紧张局势来保持自身的影响力。

• 评论提出了一种替代性的地缘政治框架，即欧盟、俄罗斯和中国合作，排除美国，形成一个独立的欧亚安全体系。

争议焦点：
• 美国对格陵兰的兴趣是否正当，以及美国是否在通过挑起地缘政治紧张来实现自身利益。

• 欧盟和加拿大是否应该以及如何排除美国，与俄罗斯和中国合作，形成一个独立的安全框架。

• 评论将美国描述为一个寻求"Lebensraum im Norden"（北方的生存空间）的国家，并将美国定位为地缘政治中的主动挑衅者，认为美国试图通过挑起战争来削弱其盟友，并使欧盟和加拿大在美国与俄罗斯之间变得无关紧要。

• 提出加拿大和欧盟应组建联盟，并与俄罗斯达成和平协议。建议欧盟制定一个欧亚安全概念，排除美国，并确保欧亚大陆国家不被海洋国家拖入战争。加拿大应参与这一过程。

• 评论暗示美国可能有更大的地缘政治目标，包括削弱其盟友和利用地缘政治紧张局势来保持自身的影响力。

• 评论提出了一种替代性的地缘政治框架，即欧盟、俄罗斯和中国合作，排除美国，形成一个独立的欧亚安全体系。

• 美国对格陵兰的兴趣是否正当，以及美国是否在通过挑起地缘政治紧张来实现自身利益。

• 欧盟和加拿大是否应该以及如何排除美国，与俄罗斯和中国合作，形成一个独立的安全框架。

data.title: France rejects backdoor mandate
data.author: hn_acker
data.article_summary: 法国国民议会明智地拒绝了旨在打击毒品 trafficking 的法案中一项危险的提案，该提案本将破坏端到端加密，迫使Signal和WhatsApp等平台允许秘密访问私人对话。在内外压力下，议员们投票否决了这项条款，赢得了数字权利、隐私和安全的胜利。该提案实际上是监视手段，企图通过"幽灵"参与者模型，让执法部门无声加入加密聊天，专家们警告这将引入系统性漏洞并损害安全通信平台的信任。法国此举为全球树立了榜样，表明无需为了公共安全牺牲基本权利，加密是现代民主和网络安全的支柱。尽管未来仍可能面临类似提案，但此次胜利显示了抵制此类措施的有效性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于在加密通讯中加入后门的讨论，涉及政治决策、技术理解、隐私保护和法律执行之间的平衡。

不同观点：
• palata：认为政治家对加密技术缺乏理解，反复要求加入后门是不理智的。尤其在欧洲，当前应加强隐私保护，而不是削弱。后门会让对手更容易获取私人数据。
• buybackoff：通过观看国民议会的辩论视频，认为内政部长Retailleau要么完全不懂技术，要么就是说谎。所谓的“选择性应用数学（加密）”是不可行的，各国都有类似的说法，试图以打击毒品交易为借口通过后门法案。
• phtrivier：指出国民议会目前分裂，部长提出后门修正案有政治动机，包括打击政敌和为未来的总统竞选造势。认为许多议员在不同政治环境下可能改变立场。
• nickslaughter02：指出虽然法国拒绝了后门，但仍支持聊天控制（设备扫描通信）。欧盟多数国家支持该提案，预计会通过。
• aucisson_masque：认为后门法案表面上针对犯罪分子，但实际上无法解决问题。犯罪分子总有办法使用其他加密方法。最终受影响的只会是普通用户。
• thomassmith65：认为公众在隐私和法律执行之间会选择后者，支持后门。预测未来某事件会导致公众要求限制E2EE（端到端加密）。
• zkmon：讨论隐私和法律执行的平衡问题，认为需要在隐私损失和执法需求之间找到可接受的平衡。
• spapas82：支持去中心化的加密方法，认为中心化的服务不可靠，使用PGP/GPG才是真正的加密通讯方式。
• ziofill：认为法国在某些方面能展现领导力。
• dickersnoodle：对新闻标题感到好笑。
• AceJohnny2：提到法国的CNIL（国家信息与自由委员会）历史悠久，旨在保护隐私。但认为CNIL现在作用有限。
• ulrikrasmussen：认为以打击毒品交易为借口通过侵犯隐私的法案是不可接受的。
• rr808：指出美国可能已经对所有信息有了后门，欧洲国家试图公平竞争但其他国家早已不守规则。建议欧洲应有自己的社交媒体公司。
• dfawcus：认为聊天控制法案可能让后门问题再次出现，战争远未结束。
• smogcutter：个人会拒绝后门法案，但尊重他人立场。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于是否应在加密通讯中加入后门以帮助执法，同时不损害普通用户的隐私。
• 政治动机和技术理解的缺乏是反对后门的主要论据。
• 欧盟内部对聊天控制法案的支持增加，可能影响未来的加密通讯政策。
• 有评论提到美国可能已经对全球信息有了广泛的访问权限，欧洲国家面临如何应对的问题。

43440513.article_content:
In a moment of clarity after initially moving forward a deeply flawed piece of legislation, the French National Assembly has done the right thing: it rejected a dangerous proposal that would have gutted end-to-end encryption in the name of fighting drug trafficking. Despite heavy pressure from the Interior Ministry,
lawmakers voted Thursday night
(article in French) to strike down a provision that would have forced messaging platforms like Signal and WhatsApp to allow hidden access to private conversations.
The vote is a victory for digital rights, for privacy and security, and for common sense.
The proposed law was a surveillance wishlist disguised as anti-drug legislation. Tucked into its text was a resurrection of the
widely discredited "ghost” participant model
—a backdoor that pretends not to be one. Under this scheme, law enforcement could silently join encrypted chats, undermining the very idea of private communication. Security experts have
condemned
the approach,
warning
it would introduce systemic vulnerabilities, damage trust in secure communication platforms, and create tools ripe for abuse.
The French lawmakers who voted this provision down deserve credit. They listened—not only to
French digital rights organizations
and technologists, but also to basic principles of cybersecurity and civil liberties. They understood that encryption protects everyone, not just activists and dissidents, but also journalists, medical professionals, abuse survivors, and ordinary citizens trying to live private lives in an increasingly surveilled world.
A Global Signal
France’s rejection of the backdoor provision should send a message to legislatures around the world: you don’t have to sacrifice fundamental rights in the name of public safety. Encryption is not the enemy of justice; it’s a tool that
supports our fundamental human rights
, including the right to have a private conversation. It is a pillar of modern democracy and cybersecurity.
As governments in the U.S., U.K., Australia, and elsewhere
continue to flirt with anti-encryption laws
, this decision should serve as a model—and a warning. Undermining encryption doesn’t make society safer. It makes everyone more vulnerable.
This victory was not inevitable. It came after sustained public pressure, expert input, and tireless advocacy from civil society. It shows that pushing back works. But for the foreseeable future, misguided lobbyists for police national security agencies will continue to push similar proposals—perhaps repackaged, or rushed through quieter legislative moments.
Supporters of privacy should celebrate this win today. Tomorrow, we will continue to keep watch.

data.title: Pen and Paper Exercises in Machine Learning (2022)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary: 这篇文章收集了一系列机器学习中的笔纸练习，涵盖线性代数、优化、有向和无向图形模型、图形模型的表达能力、因子图与消息传递、隐马尔科夫模型推理、基于模型的学习（包括独立成分分析和非标准化模型）、蒙特卡洛采样与积分以及变分推断等主题。这些练习旨在帮助学习者深入理解机器学习的核心概念和技术。相关资源和代码可以在文章关联的GitHub页面获取。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机器学习理论与实践的结合，学习资源与方法，以及对数学在机器学习中作用的看法。

不同观点：
• **理论与实践的脱节**：[lucasoshiro] 认为在学习机器学习时，理论与实践存在脱节，尤其是在选择神经元数量、层数、激活函数等实际问题上缺乏指导。他希望有人能提供理论与实践结合的资源。
• **实践资源的支持**：[simojo] 提到了Tom Yeh的"AI By Hand"练习，认为这是一个很好的实践资源，但[S4M]指出这些练习的答案紧跟在问题之后，容易让人直接看到答案而不去思考。
• **数学基础的重要性与学习方法**：[plants] 表达了对数学基础（尤其是线性代数和矩阵运算）在机器学习中重要性的关注，并寻求更多有助于打牢基础的资源，他偏好每天进行动手实践的学习方式。
• **理论与实践的必要性**：[antipaul] 质疑当前的机器学习从业者是否需要掌握这些理论知识，以及是否应该具备解决这些理论问题的能力。
• **对数学在机器学习中作用的不同看法**：[FilosofumRex] 批评了数学家在机器学习中过分强调线性代数和矩阵理论，认为学术界在某种程度上阻碍了机器学习的发展，因为过于关注符号证明而忽视了计算技术。

补充讨论：
• **对练习资源的兴趣**：[kingkongjaffa] 对更多的笔纸练习表示兴趣，尤其是针对不同主题的练习。[dang] 提到了之前在Hacker News上关于机器学习笔纸练习的讨论。[BeetleB] 对arxiv上出现此类资源表示惊讶，因为arxiv通常用于发表研究级别的论文。[axpy906] 简单表达了对资源的喜爱。[imranq] 希望有人能将这些练习转化为类似Khan Academy的自适应学习应用。

争议焦点：
• **理论与实践的平衡**：[lucasoshiro] 和 [antipaul] 质疑理论知识在实际应用中的必要性，而[FilosofumRex] 则批评学术界对理论的过分重视，认为这可能阻碍了机器学习的实际发展。

43451752.article_content:
'We use them every day': In some parts of the US, the clack of typewriter keys can still be heard
1 day ago
Share
Save
Chris Baraniuk
Share
Save
Ernesto Roman
(Credit: Ernesto Roman)
Computers and smartphones might be where most writing is done these days, but typewriters still have work to do in the US.
Pretty much every day, another customer clutching an old typewriter will walk into Mike Marr's shop in Pawtucket, Rhode Island. Marr carefully looks the machine over. Invariably, it will be a total mess. Made decades ago, the hunk of heavy metal bristling with moving parts is now laced with years of grime. The keys are too stiff. Or maybe the paper that's supposed to glide through it keeps getting stuck.
"Do you think you can get it going again?" the customer will ask, a touch of anxiety in their voice. Marr, who has been repairing typewriters for more than 20 years, will say he'll give it his best shot.
"When they come in and pick that typewriter up, just seeing their smile is everything to us," he says. Even in the year 2025, a century and a half after the
first commercially successful typewriter was introduced to the American public
, surprising numbers of people in the US are still using these machines. And not just for fun – many of Marr's customers are businesses. "We're still servicing probably 20 to 25 typewriters a week," he says. He employs three other people in his shop to keep up with the demand. "Isn't that crazy?"
In today's world, internet-connected computers and smartphones are king. They're used for the vast majority of business tasks and transactions. But here and there, in little offices and warehouses, you can still find a well-worn typewriter lingering in the corner. A machine whose keys have been pressed many thousands, if not millions, of times. To this day, typewriters print names on forms. They put addresses on envelopes. They fill out cheques. And the people who use them, generally speaking, have no intention of switching to a computer any time soon – at least for those particular tasks.
It was back in 1953 that Marr's grandfather founded the business he now runs: Marr Office Equipment. Decades ago, a call came through from IBM. The tech giant was looking for a new typewriter distributor in the northeast of the US. Marr's father and uncle, in charge at the time, were over the moon. "That was the biggest thing that could ever happen to them," says Marr. "Trailer trucks would just pull up and unload IBM after IBM. They'd already be sold. We couldn't keep up with it."
Ernesto Roman
Mike Marr has been repairing typewriters for more than 20 years and still sees dozens being brought into his shop in Rhode Island every week (Credit: Ernesto Roman)
Marr Office Equipment's heyday may be long gone but Marr still knows typewriter users all over his local area. He mentions one that is about a 10 minute drive away, in south Providence – a law firm named Tomasso & Tomasso, co-owned by brothers John and Ray, both attorneys. "We sound exactly alike," says John, laughing as he introduces himself over the phone. Do they actually still rely on typewriters? Absolutely. "There's not a day that goes by that we don't use them," says Tomasso. "This is really still the best way."
The firm's office has three typewriters, John says and his colleagues still use them to type up cheques and fill in legal forms to ensure the details on those documents are legible. Plus, there's a security angle. It's very hard to hack a typewriter since they are not connected to the internet. In 2013, jaw-dropping details emerged about the extent of US intelligence agency surveillance programmes. This prompted the
Russian Federal Guard Service (FSO) to revert to typewriters
in an attempt to evade eavesdropping. German officials were also
reported to be considering a similar move in 2014
. (During the Cold War, Soviet spies
actually developed techniques for snooping on electric typewriter activity
, a form of "keylogging" technology – where the keystrokes inputted on a keyboard are captured. US operatives also
reconstructed text from typewriter ribbons
– meaning that even typewriters aren't completely safe.)
I ask Tomasso whether there are downsides to using the typewriter – isn't it harder to correct mistakes? No, he replies, he has a model with an "eraser ribbon" that seamlessly covers up a mistype. Plus, the typewriters are inexpensive to run. Replacement ink ribbons cost around $5 (£4), he estimates. Replacement printer ink cartridges can
cost several times that
.
Besides, Tomasso loves to see his writing materialise instantly on the page in front of him. "There's more of a sense of accomplishment than just letters that appear on a screen," he explains. "It's one of those amazing devices that just makes our life better – I think that's the purpose of technology."
As a person who repairs typewriters, that's always running at the back of my mind – why are businesses still using these things? –  Paul Lundy
Further west, in Milwa

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对加密数据分块攻击的潜在解决方案与讨论

不同观点：
• [dchest] 认为可以在某种程度上解决分块问题，并分享了自己尝试过的方法——基于BuzHash的修改版本，包括伪随机替换表、基于密钥的状态初始化、窗口大小微调以及使用32位块密码对摘要进行加密。该用户还提出了通过增加填充来增加破解难度的想法，并对原文作者的工作表示赞同。

• [mananaysiempre] 提到正在探索如何使分块在可证明安全的前提下实现。他认为在不需要为每个字节计算PRF的情况下实现这一点是一个关键问题。同时，他承认总数据大小和每次传输的新数据大小是必然会泄露的信息。

• [0cf8612b2e1e] 关心此问题对使用加密分块的系统（如Restic或Borg）的实际影响，但未深入讨论具体影响和解决方案。

• [amarshall] 认为主要的漏洞来源于确定性分块和长度保持加密所导致的分块大小泄露，并建议通过在加密前添加随机长度的填充数据来缓解该问题，尽管这会增加存储和复杂性。

• [masfuerte] 提出是否可以通过随机化块的上传顺序来缓解攻击。建议在大量块上传时，通过缓冲和随机顺序上传减轻攻击效果。

• [jszymborski] 建议使用SipHash来缓解问题，认为其可以通过密钥防止已知明文攻击，但同时也担心其性能问题。随后，他提到了使用键控滚动哈希作为替代方案。

• [ThomasWaldmann] 提供了关于Borg备份的讨论链接，指向GitHub上的讨论页面，将讨论引向具体项目实现。

• [pbsd] 关注技术细节，对文章中的数学模型（特别是环R和映射p）提出问题，表明其关注点在于理论基础的准确性。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及多个潜在缓解策略，包括算法改进（如SipHash、滚动哈希）、随机化（填充长度、块上传顺序）、以及对具体项目（如Borg和Restic）的实际影响。
- 争议焦点在于如何在保证效率的前提下实现分块攻击的有效缓解，特别是在实际应用中如何平衡安全性和性能。

data.title: StarVector: Generating Scalable Vector Graphics Code from Images and Text
data.author: lnyan
data.article_summary: StarVector是一种基于视觉-语言模型架构的基础模型，用于从图像和文本指令生成可缩放矢量图形（SVG）代码。它通过将矢量化任务视为代码生成问题，突破了传统图像处理的局限，能够生成包括圆形、多边形、文本元素和复杂路径的高质量SVG。StarVector依赖于多模态架构，能够精确处理视觉和文本信息，生成复杂的SVG元素，并在SVG-Stack数据集和SVG-Bench评估框架上进行了广泛训练和验证。该模型在文本到SVG和图像到SVG生成任务中显著优于现有方法，提供了领先的复杂图形处理能力和多样化的图形风格支持。StarVector作为开源资源，为高品质矢量图形生成设立了新标准。

Figure 1:
StarVector is a foundation model for SVG generation. It uses a Vision-Language Modeling architecture
to understand images and text instructions. StarVector excels at vectorizing a wide range of visual
inputs, from general icons and logotypes to more intricate vectors such as technical diagrams.
StarVector represents a breakthrough in Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) generation, seamlessly integrating visual and textual inputs into a unified foundation SVG model. By reframing vectorization as a code generation task rather than a traditional image processing problem, StarVector transcends previous limitations. This paradigm shift enables the model to leverage the full richness of SVG syntax—including circles, polygons, text elements, and complex paths—without simplification. Our approach allows training on internet-scale data to capture the diverse spectrum of vector representations. At its core, the model employs a vision-language architecture (VLM), enabling unprecedented capabilities in generating complex SVG elements. Complemented by SVG-Stack—our extensive dataset—and SVG-Bench—our comprehensive evaluation framework—StarVector establishes a new paradigm for high-quality vector graphics generation.
Key Capabilities
01
Advanced Multimodal Architecture
StarVector's multimodal architecture processes both visual and textual information with remarkable precision, enabling sophisticated image vectorization and text-guided SVG creation that captures fine details and structural relationships. The image encoder and language decoder work together to understand the semantics of an image in pixel space, recognizing primitive shapes, hierarchies, and layers to produce compact and semantically meaningful SVG primitive outputs.
02
Unparalleled Complexity Handling
Where traditional algorithms falter, StarVector excels—effortlessly recognizing and generating intricate SVG elements including text, complex paths, and various primitives directly from images. The model intelligently identifies geometric shapes, connectivity patterns, and structural elements to produce professional-quality diagrams and icons.
03
Robust Data Foundation
Built upon SVG-Stack—our meticulously curated dataset of over 2 million SVG samples—and evaluated through SVG-Bench, StarVector benefits from diverse, high-quality training examples that ensure consistent performance across various graphic styles and complexities.
04
Leading-Edge Performance
StarVector significantly outperforms existing methods in both text-to-SVG and image-to-SVG generation tasks, demonstrating a substantial leap forward in vectorization quality while remaining fully accessible to the research community as an open-source resource.
Model Architecture
StarVector employs a vision-language architecture to generate high-quality SVG code
Figure 2: a) StarVector Architecture:
StarVector projects images into embeddings via an image encoder,
then maps these embeddings to the LLM hidden space using an LLM Adapter, generating Visual Tokens.
Text conditioning is achieved with the LLM's tokenizer and embedder. The model learns to map token
sequences (visual or textual) to SVG code. The symbol ⊕ denotes mutually exclusive operations (image-to-
SVG or text-to-SVG), while ‖ indicates sequence concatenation.
Figure 2: b)Vision Model and Adapter:
The
image encoder employs a Vision Transformer (ViT) to process image patches sequentially. The LLM Adapter
non-linearly projects embeddings into visual tokens for LLM integration.
The architecture shown above enables StarVector to process both images and text prompts through a unified framework. This approach allows the model to leverage the strengths of both modalities, resulting in more accurate and contextually appropriate SVG generation. The LLM Adapter is a critical component that bridges the gap between visual and textual representations, ensuring that the model can effectively translate visual information into structured SVG code.

data.title: Global population datasets underrepresent rural population
data.author: croes
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了全球网格化人口数据集在农村地区的系统性低估问题。通过分析35个国家307个大坝建设项目导致的居民搬迁数据，研究发现，WorldPop、GWP、GRUMP、LandScan和GHS-POP等数据集在农村地区存在显著负偏差，低估幅度从53%到84%不等。这表明，即使在最准确的数据集中，农村人口也被低估了一半。为了确保农村社区公平获取服务和资源，必须对数据集的应用进行审视。改进措施包括加强人口普查、替代人口统计方法以及更均衡的人口模型校准。

43398308.article_content:
Global gridded population datasets systematically underrepresent rural population
Download PDF
Download PDF
Subjects
Geography
Scientific data
Socioeconomic scenarios
Sustainability
Water resources
Abstract
Numerous initiatives towards sustainable development rely on global gridded population data. Such data have been calibrated primarily for urban environments, but their accuracy in the rural domain remains largely unexplored. This study systematically validates global gridded population datasets in rural areas, based on reported human resettlement from 307 large dam construction projects in 35 countries. We find large discrepancies between the examined datasets, and, without exception, significant negative biases of −53%, −65%, −67%, −68%, and −84% for WorldPop, GWP, GRUMP, LandScan, and GHS-POP, respectively. This implies that rural population is, even in the most accurate dataset, underestimated by half compared to reported figures. To ensure equitable access to services and resources for rural communities, past and future applications of the datasets must undergo a critical discussion in light of the identified biases. Improvements in the datasets’ accuracies in rural areas can be attained through strengthened population censuses, alternative population counts, and a more balanced calibration of population models.

and disaster risk management

. In recent years, the advancement of geospatial technologies and the widespread availability of satellite imagery and remote sensing data have facilitated the development of global gridded population data
12
,
13
. These comprehensive datasets partition the planet into evenly spaced, high-resolution grid cells with population counts, enabling researchers and policy makers to gain insights into the spatial distribution of human populations on a global scale (Fig.
1
).

shows an enlargement of panel d. Country boundary courtesy of ©EuroGeographics.
Full size image
To date, eight open-access datasets of population counts are available with (near-)global coverage, namely GWP (Gridded Population of the World)
14
, GRUMP (Global Rural-Urban Mapping Project)
15
, GHS-POP (Global Human Settlement Population)
16
, LandScan
17
, WorldPop
18
, HYDE (History database of the Global Environment)
19
, HRSL (High Resolution Settlement Layer)
20
, and Kontur
21
(Table
1
). The models behind these products have varying degrees of complexity, ranging from simple areal disaggregation of census counts (as in GWP
14
) to dasymetric mapping approaches involving numerous auxiliary data sources, such as satellite-based detection of infrastructures and nightlights (as in WorldPop
18
). Details of the population datasets and their underlying methods are documented by Leyk et al.

, TReNDS
13
, and on the website of the POPGRID data collaborative (
https://www.popgrid.org
).

Due to their large spatial coverage and relevance for countless disciplines, the use and application of global gridded population datasets has dramatically increased in recent years
22
, but a consistent global-scale assessment of their accuracy is to date lacking. The datasets have been primarily validated and assessed in scattered countries or regions
22
,

data.author: nanna
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Liberapay平台的优缺点及使用体验

不同观点：
• **支持Liberapay的简约和非商业化特性**：  
  - internetter认为Liberapay没有花哨的功能，但感觉更像是朋友间的交换，而不是商业关系。他们不喜欢分级奖励机制，因为这带来了额外劳动的期望。
  - culi也支持Liberapay，因为创作者可以获得100%的收入，不像Patreon会收取12-16%的费用。

• **Liberapay的局限性**：  
  - internetter提到Liberapay的Stripe集成有问题，只能使用PayPal，且PayPal不自动续费，导致潜在收入损失。
  - culi指出Liberapay缺乏Patreon那样的分级权限整合，这对某些创作者可能是个问题。

• **推广和使用建议**：  
  - patcon和daghamm都希望更多人使用Liberapay，特别是欧盟用户，认为它比Patreon和GitHub Sponsors更好。
  - nanna列出了一些Liberapay上与Emacs相关的账户，鼓励社区支持。

• **税务和费用问题**：  
  - smallerfish询问Liberapay是否提供501c3免税捐赠选项，因为他们的基金会需要为美国捐赠者提供税务优惠。
  - bullen希望Liberapay能设置固定价格的 recurring payment items。
  - bsnnkv询问Liberapay是否提供美国报税所需的税务表格。

• **其他支付系统对比和建议**：  
  - lazzlazzlazz提到支付处理费用问题，建议考虑stablecoins以减少费用。
  - webspinner认为Liberapay是Patreon的不错替代品。
  - amryl询问Liberapay与GNU Taler支付系统的比较。

• **隐私和加密货币支持**：  
  - DrNosferatu询问是否可以隐藏收入。
  - 3x3m3询问是否支持比特币捐赠。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中提到了Flattr的关闭（seltzered_），以及Liberapay的GitHub项目页面（brianzelip），显示了对类似平台历史和其他开源项目的关注。

争议焦点：
- Liberapay是否应增加更多功能（如固定价格的 recurring payment items）以满足不同用户的需求，同时保持其简约和非商业化的特性。

data.title: Powers of 2 with all even digits
data.author: Hbruz0
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于2的幂次结果为全偶数位数的数学现象及其性质探讨

不同观点：
• nneonneo分享了一个有趣的发现，指出2^133477987019是末尾有40个偶数位数的最小2的幂次，且该数有超过400亿个数字。他还提到自己编写了一个搜索程序，能够在几分钟内计算到2^(10^13)，但内存受限。同时，他指出在2^15258789062500范围内没有找到其他全偶数位数的数。
• bluewin提到曾和朋友研究过2的幂次个位数的循环模式，并开发了一个可以生成任意底数幂次的系统。他们还研究了数字频率分解，发现了一些类似于核磁共振（NMR）的共振现象。
• WithinReason引用了Michael S. Branicky的结果，指出在2^(10^10)范围内没有新的全偶数位数的结果。
• waffletower讨论了在十六进制和八进制下，2的幂次末尾全为偶数的现象，认为由于基数表示和序列交互的原因，这种现象不会是有限的。
• hrldcpr简单指出，在二进制下这种数根本不存在。
• andrewla表示对这种简单性质缺乏证明感到惊讶，认为尽管2048可能是最高这样的幂次，但证明这一点似乎并不简单。
• IsTom认为这个序列可能是有限的，但也有可能是一个“快速增长序列”。
• Mae_soph尝试给出一个证明，通过分析2的幂次的进位情况，认为可以证明这个序列是完整的，但其证明过程较为复杂且涉及较多假设。
• Aardwolf指出在二进制下不存在这样的数，因为所有的二进制表示都是以1000...的形式存在。
• openasocket提到筛理论（Sieve theory）可能是研究这一序列性质的一个相关数学工具。
• lanna提问有多少2的幂次只有单个偶数位数，并列举了一些例子。
• vanderZwan表示希望看到一个关于这个现象的Numberphile节目，并认为通过数学爱好者的关注可能会很快得出这个序列是否有限的证明。
• darepublic询问是否存在除暴力搜索外的其他方法来研究这个问题。
• jmount提到了一个关于数字排列的简单问题，并给出了一个链接。
• bitwize提到33554432（2^25）是一个全偶数位数的数，并分享了其在80年代计算器上的趣事。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多种基数下的情况，如十六进制和八进制，并探讨了这些基数下的全偶数位数现象。
• 有人提到通过编写程序进行大规模搜索，但受限于内存和计算资源。
• 关于是否存在除暴力搜索外的其他研究方法，讨论中没有明确答案，但提到了一些可能的数学工具和理论，如筛理论。
• 有人尝试给出数学证明，但证明过程复杂且涉及较多假设，尚未得到广泛认可。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于这个序列是否有限，有人认为可能是有限的，但也有观点认为可能是一个“快速增长序列”。
• 另外，关于是否存在除暴力搜索外的其他研究方法，讨论中没有明确结论。

总结：
讨论围绕2的幂次全为偶数位数的现象展开，涉及多种基数下的情况、搜索程序的应用、可能的数学证明和研究方法等。参与者分享了各自的研究发现和观点，但尚未得出明确的结论。

• tompccs：认为该软件针对的市场与Xero和Quickbooks不同，后两者主要面向小型企业（如个体经营者、咖啡馆、理发店等），而新软件似乎更专注于需要复杂财务分析工具的小公司。同时指出，通过赢得高街会计师的青睐可以扩大市场份额。
• pierotofy：关注软件的退出策略和数据可移植性，建议考虑开放源代码业务模式，并指出当前定价高于Xero的入门计划。
• internet101010 和 WorldMaker：强调Excel在财务报告中的主导地位，指出新软件需要与Excel高度兼容，包括导出功能和Excel插件。WorldMaker特别提到Excel是中小型企业会计软件的最大竞争对手。
• aurumque：对QuickBooks的质量下降和价格上涨感到不满，认为新软件有机会打破市场垄断，"无弹窗广告的QuickBooks"是一个吸引人的卖点。
• christoff12：作为一名会计硕士生和CPA考生，关注软件的长期承诺和Excel的兼容性，并计划推荐给其工作的 fractional CFO 公司。
• curun1r：基于在Intuit的工作经验，指出会计师在产品设计中的重要性，Quickbooks的UI尽管不直观，但其复杂性反而成为一种“护城河”，专业会计师不愿意改变。
• mritchie712：指出外包会计的普遍性，特别是在VC支持的初创公司中，企业主不太可能亲自使用会计软件。
• epistasis：对QuickBooks不满，对新软件感兴趣，但不清楚“Linear”是什么。
• nicksiscoe 和 keizo：讨论自建同步引擎与使用现成解决方案的决策，并希望有更多的定价透明度和对中小企业的适用性。
• throwaway667555：认为集成电子表格是杀手级功能，并提到MS Dynamics可能提供类似功能。
• markhalonen：引用PC Mag 1995年的文章，指出会计软件多年来变化不大。
• tntpreneur 和 seddona：对“Linear”被广泛提及感到惊讶，并建议开放核心公司模式，提供SQL数据库的直接访问和代码自定义能力。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于新软件的市场定位和定价策略。有人认为其针对小公司市场可能较小，且定价高于竞品如Xero。
• Excel在财务领域的广泛使用被多次提及，强调了与Excel兼容的重要性。
• 专业会计师在会计软件选择中的影响力被强调，Quickbooks的复杂UI被视为一种专业壁垒。
• 开放源代码和数据可移植性被一些评论者视为重要功能，特别是对于技术背景的用户。

data.title: How I accepted myself into Canada's largest AI hackathon
data.author: fastcall
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者参加GenAI Genesis 2025黑客松前，意外发现活动网站存在安全漏洞的经历。作者在注册账号后因密码未保存而重置密码，随后意识到网站使用了Firebase，并回忆起有关Firebase配置不当的案例。通过分析网站前端代码，作者获取了Firebase配置信息并尝试访问数据库，虽然初始尝试未果，但最终发现网站会在提交申请时抓取所有用户数据并解析。利用这一设计缺陷，作者成功通过更新数据库中的申请状态字段，将自己标记为"已接受"，从而在申请截止前"通过"了自己的申请。

, a generative AI hackathon hosted at my school, the University of Toronto, I decided to apply even though I was pretty busy that weekend, hoping my schedule would clear by the time the hackathon came around. The sequence of events that followed led me into finding a vulnerability that let me accept my own hackathon application, before applications had even officially closed.
story time!

After making my account on the site at 3 o’clock in the morning, I somehow realized that I had better things to do at the time (like sleeping), and so I decided to apply the following day. Oddly, my password manager (KeePassXC for those curious), didn’t save my password and I had to reset it:

articles

data.title: Oxygen atoms discovered in most distant known galaxy
data.author: sohkamyung
data.article_summary: 天文学家利用阿塔卡马大型毫米/亚毫米阵列（ALMA）在已知最遥远的星系JADES-GS-z14-0中发现了氧气。这一发现表明，该星系在宇宙诞生不到3亿年时已经化学成熟，比预期更早形成和成熟。通常，星系初期主要由氢和氦组成，重元素如氧气在恒星演化后形成并扩散。然而，JADES-GS-z14-0的氧气含量比预期高出约10倍，挑战了以往关于星系形成速度的认知。ALMA的精确测量将该星系的距离确定到红移约14.18，并展示了与詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜（JWST）协同观测早期星系的潜力。这一发现揭示了宇宙中首批星系的形成条件。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对早期宇宙中氧元素发现的相关讨论

不同观点：
• PaulHoule认为，根据Webb的观察，宇宙在最初的十亿年里发展得比我们预想的要快，实际上可能有五十亿年。这暗示了当前对宇宙年龄的理解可能有误。
• divbzero支持PaulHoule的观点，并提出两种可能性：要么是核合成理论不完整，要么是宇宙比我们想象的更古老，并质疑当前模型中的假设或参数是否准确。
• ck2指出，该发现中的氧元素来源于成熟恒星释放的重元素，而非植物生命，并提到氧气检测的难度，同时分享了一个关于新检测方法的链接。
• gentle批评了那些质疑科学家和文章作者的评论者，认为这些评论者没有认真阅读相关链接，并表现出无知。

补充讨论：
• joquarky和hsnewman认为氧气和氢气在宇宙中无处不在，发现氧元素并不令人惊讶，甚至认为这是理所当然的结果。
• interludead对在如此年轻的星系中发现氧元素表示惊讶，认为这是非常惊人的发现。
• fasteo将讨论引向更广泛的宇宙起源问题，询问大爆炸理论是否是科学界的共识，并探讨可能的替代理论。
• shemtay指出文章并未暗示发现的是分子氧，建议将标题改为“氧元素”或“原子氧”，以避免误解。
• EGreg质疑科学家如何确定检测到的确实是氧元素。

Oxygen discovered in most distant known galaxy
20 March 2025
Two different teams of astronomers have detected oxygen in the most distant known galaxy, JADES-GS-z14-0. The discovery, reported in two separate studies, was made possible thanks to the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA), in which the European Southern Observatory (ESO) is a partner. This record-breaking detection is making astronomers rethink how quickly galaxies formed in the early Universe.
Discovered last year
, JADES-GS-z14-0 is the most distant confirmed galaxy ever found: it is so far away, its light took 13.4 billion years to reach us, meaning we see it as it was when the Universe was less than 300 million years old, about 2% of its present age. The new oxygen detection with
ALMA
, a telescope array in Chile’s Atacama Desert, suggests the galaxy is much more chemically mature than expected.
“
It is like finding an adolescent where you would only expect babies
,” says Sander Schouws, a PhD candidate at Leiden Observatory, the Netherlands, and first author of the Dutch-led study, now accepted for publication in
The Astrophysical Journal
. “
The results show the galaxy has formed very rapidly and is also maturing rapidly, adding to a growing body of evidence that the formation of galaxies happens much faster than was expected
."
Galaxies usually start their lives full of young stars, which are made mostly of light elements like hydrogen and helium. As stars evolve, they create heavier elements like oxygen, which get dispersed through their host galaxy after they die. Researchers had thought that, at 300 million years old, the Universe was still too young to have galaxies ripe with heavy elements. However, the two ALMA studies indicate JADES-GS-z14-0 has about 10 times more heavy elements than expected.
“
I was astonished by the unexpected results because they opened a new view on the first phases of galaxy evolution
,” says Stefano Carniani, of the Scuola Normale Superiore of Pisa, Italy, and lead author on the paper now accepted for publication in
Astronomy & Astrophysics
. “
The evidence that a galaxy is already mature in the infant Universe raises questions about when and how galaxies formed
.”
The oxygen detection has also allowed astronomers to make their distance measurements to JADES-GS-z14-0 much more accurate. “
The ALMA detection offers an extraordinarily precise measurement of the galaxy’s distance down to an uncertainty of just 0.005 percent. This level of precision — analogous to being accurate within 5 cm over a distance of 1 km — helps refine our understanding of distant galaxy properties
,” adds Eleonora Parlanti, a PhD student at the Scuola Normale Superiore of Pisa and author on the
Astronomy & Astrophysics
study
[1]
.
“
While the galaxy was originally discovered with the
James Webb Space Telescope
, it took ALMA to confirm and precisely determine its enormous distance
,”
[2]
says Associate Professor Rychard Bouwens, a member of the team at Leiden Observatory. “
This shows the amazing synergy between ALMA and JWST to reveal the formation and evolution of the first galaxies
.”
Gergö Popping, an ESO astronomer at the European ALMA Regional Centre who did not take part in the studies, says:
"I was really surprised by this clear detection of oxygen in JADES-GS-z14-0. It suggests galaxies can form more rapidly after the Big Bang than had previously been thought. This result showcases the important role ALMA plays in unraveling the conditions under which the first galaxies in our Universe formed."
Notes
[1] Astronomers use a measurement known as
redshift
to determine the distance to extremely distant objects. Previous measurements indicated that the galaxy JADES-GS-z-14-0 was at a redshift between about 14.12 and 14.4. With their oxygen detections, both teams have now narrowed this down to a redshift around 14.18.
[2] The James Webb Space Telescope is a joint project of NASA, the European Space Agency (ESA) and the Canadian Space Agency (CSA).
More information
This research was presented in two papers to appear in
Astronomy & Astrophysics (
https://aanda.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202452451
)
and
The Astrophysical Journal.
The teams are composed of:
